## Design

### 2026-10-05 — October 5th: Starbie schematic, footprints and routing, and a lot of KiCad errors

**5h**

October 5th: Starbie schematic, footprints and routing, and a lot of KiCad errors
Today I set up the whole Starbie project and wanted to get the schematic finished and see how far I could get with the PCB. I followed the Half-Life week 1 guide, but I'd never used KiCad before, so a big part of the session went into fixing things that didn't work.

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 130358](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/CpZKBREdtQJpg3Zd0ZnE3GL2jRbYLFgg/5f2ba0c985272eb033a70994fbd0a7b3b0a24714b29080a6f723dd287818364b.png)
First I set up the GitHub repo with the folders from the shipping guide (cad, pcb, firmware and assets), plus a README and this journal.
The XIAO symbol wouldn't load
I imported the Care Package libraries, but KiCad said the Seeed_Studio_XIAO_Series library was made with a newer version (file format from October 2025 or later). My KiCad was too old, so I updated to KiCad 10.0.6, and that fixed it
 Finding the footprints
The imported footprints (the display, MPU6050 and XIAO) only show up if the .pretty folder is added with the nickname "Imported Parts". Once that was right, I could assign all of them in the footprint assignment tool.

Layout and routing
I drew the board outline on the Edge.Cuts layer and placed all the parts inside it. Then I routed everything and added a ground pour.

Running the DRC
The only errors left were two "malformed courtyard" errors on J1, the display footprint. The guide says to ignore these, so I excluded them. There were 0 unconnected items.
Whenever I got stuck, I searched on Google and YouTube first. Only when I really couldn't figure it out did I ask an AI to explain it.
tl;dr: Finished the schematic, footprints, layout and routing, and fixed the KiCad version, library and footprint errors.
Next: Export the Gerbers, make a BOM, write the firmware and add a render to the README.
Time spent this session: 5 hours
